notes.observation: The chapter explicitly returns to the anti-Hindi movement begun in 1938 and Kalaignar's place among the 'தமிழர் படை', continuing terminology already established in v1-ch06.

notes.observation: Alagirisami's speech is rendered through active public-speech images: a storm on stage, revolutionary sound reaching the sky, and a roar like a thousand lions. The scene then turns abruptly to vomiting blood, collapse and pain.
notes.translation_action: Preserve the accumulation, abrupt tonal turn and bodily cost of the speech. Do not summarize the episode as merely an inspiring meeting.

notes.observation: In Alagirisami's direct speech the stable source/page-witness wording is 'டாக்டருக்கு ஜலதோஷம் என்பதற்காக ஜன்னி பிறந்தவனைக் கவனிக்காமலிருக்கலாமா?' The internal corpus search did not supply a separate precedent for the period medical term 'ஜன்னி'; the broad contrast is secure (a doctor with a minor cold versus a much more seriously ill patient), but the exact lexical diagnosis is not yet fixed.
notes.translation_action: Do not silently emend the stable source wording or invent a precise modern diagnosis. T1 may preserve the severe-illness contrast conservatively; resolve the exact English handling of 'ஜன்னி' with lexical evidence by T2/terminology review.

notes.observation: Kalaignar moves from handwritten student publishing to wanting his writing on the 'vehicle of print', then names Arignar Anna's 'திராவிடநாடு' journal. He says his article appeared in either the third or fourth issue, and later names the article 'இளமைப் பலி!' and the unpublished follow-up 'பகுத்தறிவு பரமசிவம்'.
notes.translation_action: Preserve Dravida Nadu as a publication title, retain the author's deliberate 'third or fourth issue' uncertainty, and keep both article titles visibly as titles. Do not manufacture a precise issue number.

notes.observation: Looking back on his first meeting with Anna, Kalaignar says Anna continued for 'more than 27 years' as an elder-brother figure and ideal. The passage deliberately measures the relationship from the narrator's retrospective present.
notes.translation_action: Preserve the relative duration as authored. Do not convert it into inferred calendar endpoints.

notes.translation_action: Keep the quoted formulation visibly quoted and preserve the visual/emotional staging; do not replace it with an external canonical English version.

notes.observation: The Tamil Nadu Tamil Students' Association fundraiser stages Kalaignar's 'பழனியப்பன்': cost 200 rupees, collection 80 rupees because of heavy rain, debt exceeding 100 rupees, creditors surrounding the theatre, an actress owed salary/travel money, and a silver cup worth 20 rupees given to send her home.
notes.translation_action: Preserve the amounts, causal sequence, theatre materiality and short rhetorical questions. Do not compress the episode into a generic statement that the play lost money.

notes.observation: At Nagapattinam, Dravidar Kazhagam leader R. V. Gopal ultimately pays 100 rupees for 'பழனியப்பன்' for the planned Nagai Dravidian Actors' Association. The memoir then says the first play was staged elsewhere as 'சாந்தா' and later as 'நச்சுக் கோப்பை'.
notes.translation_action: Preserve the organizational role, the 100-rupee sale and the authored title-history sequence Palaniyappan → Santa → Natchuk Koppai. Do not collapse the three titles into one or silently modernize institutional names.

notes.observation: Kalaignar says a love relationship failed principally because he was a 'சுயமரியாதைக்காரன்'; the woman then married another man under priestly rites. His family subsequently seeks an immediate marriage for him.
notes.translation_action: Preserve Self-Respect political identity and the contrast with priestly marriage rites. Do not neutralize the ideological cause of the failed relationship.
